messages:
Nina P.: Quick heads upwe're trialing a 'short-wait' handoff to reduce bad-owner incidents. Canary at 20% in 12m. Share your watchpoints.
Carlos V.: What's the wait threshold? want to avoid slowing down response for hot leads.
Leah H.: Suggest 25s wait for enrichment flag then fallback to RR overflow. Tag fallback_reason=ENRICH_TIMEOUT and add property lead.source_canary=true.
Tom B.: Can we set a soft alert at 18s so SDRs can optionally take manual handoff? keep it off by default for canary.
Nina P.: Yes, soft alert only for SDRs who opt-in. For canary leads we'll also pause automated email drips until owner confirmed.
Carlos V.: HubSpot workflow snippet for docs:
```
Trigger: new contact
Delay: 25s
If: property(enriched)==true -> Smart assign owner
Else -> Assign to queue: Overflow RR; set property(fallback_reason)=ENRICH_TIMEOUT; set property(source_canary)=true
```
Leah H.: Salesforce mapping: create boolean field fallback_flag and keep original owner null on fallback to preserve attribution.
HubSpot Bot: Workflow "ShortWait Handoff Canary" created by Carlos V. (ID 19999)
Tom B.: I'll spin up a small dashboard: assign_latency_p95, enrichment_success_rate, fallback_rate. Page if fallback_rate > 0.12 for 10m.
Nina P.: Runbook: mute expected alerts, notify SDR rotation, verify webhook secrets. We'll do a 15m check-in after canary start.
Carlos V.: Pushing the flag in 10m, will post link to dashboard once live.
Leah H.: FYI if enrichment pipeline backpressure detected we'll auto-shorten wait to 10s per autoscaler signal.
Nina P.: Thanks everyone. tagging @here 3m before go. DM me if you need escalation contact.
